isatvon_definition.i_instructions: Triggered by the Dify DMR's POST /tool/execute for skill_index 7 of Standard_BOM_Flow, after resolve_final_selection has cleared. Action: require cbom_db.cbom rows to already exist (hard ValueError otherwise); clear any prior report rows for this rfq_id across all 16 report tables (report_generator.clear_reports_rfq); then, inside one transaction, iterate constants.REPORT_ORDER (a hardcoded list of 16 report table names) and execute one INSERT-SQL statement per report. Check: if ANY of the 16 reports raises an exception during its INSERT, that failure is collected into an issues list, and the caller (run_pipeline) raises RuntimeError, rolling back the ENTIRE transaction -- no partial report set is ever left committed. Bound: single attempt at the whole-batch level, no retry loop; the 16-report loop is a fan-out over distinct, independent reports, not a retry of one action. Business rule: does NOT regenerate cbom itself -- reads whatever cbom data already exists for the rfq_id.

fresh_state_parameters: cbom_db.cbom rows for this rfq_id -- REQUIRED precondition; raises ValueError 'No cbom rows found... call the cbom tool first' otherwise
cbom_db.cbom.final_price_conv IS NOT NULL row count -- used only to compute a warning, not a gate
Whether any of the 16 report tables already has rows for this rfq_id -- unconditionally cleared before regeneration, so this is always a full regenerate, never incremental

a_automation.action_step: BEGIN TRANSACTION; report_generator.clear_reports_rfq(con, rfq_id); report_generator.generate_reports(con, rfq_id) -- internally: build 2 shared SQL views (selected_quote_sql, ex_inv_calc_sql), then for table in constants.REPORT_ORDER: execute that report's INSERT-SQL and record its row count, catching any per-report exception into an issues list rather than stopping the loop immediately.
a_automation.acceptance_check: Programmatically evaluate whether reports_result['issues'] is empty; if non-empty, run_pipeline raises RuntimeError and the whole transaction is rolled back -- an all-or-nothing commit, not a partial-success outcome.

t_tech_stack.action_tool: generate_reports (this tool itself, delegating to reporting_pipeline.run_pipeline -> report_generator.generate_reports/clear_reports_rfq)
t_tech_stack.fixed_check_tool: None -- no independent validation MCP tool exists; the cbom-rows precondition and the per-report issue collection are both inline logic within reporting_pipeline.py/report_generator.py themselves.

v_variables.success_gate: reports_result['issues'] is empty -- all 16 of constants.REPORT_ORDER's INSERT-SQL statements executed without exception
v_variables.no_op_condition: None -- every call unconditionally clears and regenerates all 16 report tables for the rfq_id; there is no already-processed short-circuit
v_variables.escalation_condition: A single report's SQL failure aborts and rolls back the entire batch (RuntimeError, surfaced as status:'failed' with the failing table names/errors) -- there is no hitl gate here; this is a hard failure, not a human-review pause
v_variables.budget_limit: 300s MCP Jungle call_tool() timeout / 600s Dify HTTP node timeout

json_schema.report_row_counts: object mapping each of the 16 report table names to its row count (or null if it failed)
json_schema.issues: array of {table, error} objects -- always empty on a successfully committed run, since any non-empty issues list triggers a rollback+raise instead of a returned response

o_outcome.state_handoff_file: No dedicated append-only audit table exists. Real state handoff is: (1) the 16 report tables' rows in reports.duckdb, (2) one logger.info(...) line to report_generation.log capturing the full summary (cbom_rows, per-table counts, warnings, issues), (3) PostHog report_generated/report_generation_failed events bucketed by duration and report count.
